articles.headline: OFAC Issues Counter Narcotics and Cyber-related Designations, Amends Russia-related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and cyber-related activities. This action underscores the U.S. government's commitment to disrupting illicit networks that pose threats to national security and financial stability.

In addition to the new designations, OFAC issued an Illicit Drugs General License and an amended Russia-related General License. The amended Russia-related General License, along with new Frequently Asked Questions, aims to provide clarity and guidance to stakeholders regarding permissible activities under the existing sanctions regime.
These measures are part of ongoing efforts to combat the flow of illicit drugs and counter malicious cyber activities, while also refining the implementation of sanctions against Russia.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals for Counter Terrorism Activities
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced new designations under its counter terrorism authority. These actions target individuals and entities found to be involved in supporting terrorist organizations and their activities globally.
The designations aim to disrupt financial networks and logistical support structures that enable terrorist groups to operate and carry out their illicit agendas.
This move reinforces the U.S. government's commitment to combating terrorism and safeguarding the international financial system from abuse by malign actors.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced a new round of designations targeting individuals and entities engaged in both counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities. This dual focus highlights the interconnected nature of these illicit networks.
These designations aim to sever financial and logistical ties that enable drug trafficking organizations and terrorist groups to operate and expand their influence.
The U.S. Treasury continues to leverage its sanctions authorities to protect the U.S. financial system from abuse and to counter threats to national security.

articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran Designation Information
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued an update regarding existing Iran designations. This action involves modifications to the identifying information of previously sanctioned individuals and entities.

While no new designations were announced, these updates are crucial for ensuring the accuracy and effectiveness of the Iran sanctions program. They help financial institutions and other regulated entities to maintain compliance.
The U.S. Treasury continues to monitor and adapt its sanctions against Iran to address ongoing proliferation concerns and destabilizing activities in the region.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-related Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced new designations targeting individuals and entities involved in Iran-related activities. These actions are part of the U.S. government's ongoing efforts to pressure the Iranian regime.
The designations aim to disrupt networks supporting Iran's destabilizing activities, including its nuclear program, ballistic missile development, and support for regional proxy groups.
These measures reinforce the comprehensive U.S. sanctions regime against Iran, emphasizing the commitment to preventing the regime from acquiring resources for its illicit activities.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities for Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Activities, Expands Cuba Sanctions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced new designations targeting entities involved in cyber-related activities and transnational criminal organizations. These actions aim to disrupt malicious cyber actors and criminal networks that pose a threat to U.S. national security and economic interests.

Additionally, OFAC imposed new Cuba designations and published a Cuba-related determination. These measures expand the scope of U.S. sanctions against Cuba, targeting key sectors of the Cuban economy and individuals supporting the regime.

The determination extends Executive Order 14404 to four additional sectors of the Cuban economy: manufacturing, technology, electronics, and marine, paving the way for further designations in these areas.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-related Designations, Issues Alert, and Amends Venezuela-related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced new Iran-related designations and updates to certain Iran-related listings. These actions are part of a broader strategy to counter the Iranian regime's illicit activities and its support for terrorism.

OFAC also published an Iran-related alert, specifically warning about the Iranian shadow fleet's reliance on false flags for sanctions evasion. This alert aims to increase awareness and vigilance among maritime stakeholders to prevent circumvention of sanctions.
Furthermore, an amended Venezuela-related General License and a new Frequently Asked Question were issued, providing updated guidance on permissible transactions involving Venezuela.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced the issuance of an amended Iran-related General License. This amendment modifies existing authorizations related to transactions involving Iran.

General Licenses are issued to authorize certain categories of transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under U.S. sanctions programs. This amendment aims to provide clarity or adjust the scope of permissible activities.
Stakeholders involved in Iran-related transactions should review the amended General License carefully to ensure ongoing compliance with U.S. sanctions regulations.

articles.region: North Korea / Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Imposes North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo-related Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced new designations targeting individuals and entities connected to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. These actions are part of ongoing efforts to counter illicit activities in both regions.

The North Korea designations aim to disrupt networks supporting the regime's weapons of mass destruction programs and other destabilizing actions. The Democratic Republic of the Congo-related designations target those involved in corruption and human rights abuses.
These measures underscore the U.S. government's commitment to promoting stability and accountability globally through the strategic use of financial sanctions.

articles.headline: EU Expands Russia Sanctions, Designating 113 Individuals and Entities
body: The Council of the European Union has added 113 individuals and entities to its principal Russia sanctions list, with an additional 32 listings under its hybrid and cyber sanctions regimes. These measures are in response to Russia's continued aggression against Ukraine, particularly its attacks on civilian infrastructure.

The new designations extend restrictions across banking, energy, shipping, and online retail, targeting nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions. This aims to further cut off financial channels that fund Russia's war effort and support its shadow fleet.

Among the newly sanctioned are the sole shareholder of Russian retail giant Wildberries and an individual controlling a majority stake in Ozon, another major Russian e-commerce company. The EU also imposed sanctions on 30 individuals and two entities for Russia's foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI) and malicious cyber activities.

The Mansudae Overseas Project Group of Companies is known for its involvement in exporting workers from the DPRK to other nations for construction-related activities, including the creation of statues and monuments, to generate revenue for the DPRK government or the Workers' Party of Korea.

articles.headline: IMF Head Warns AI Demand Will Drive Global Interest Rate Hikes
body: Kristalina Georgieva, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), has warned that booming demand for artificial intelligence (AI) will compel central banks worldwide to raise interest rates. Speaking at the 2026 Apec summit in Shenzhen, Georgieva stated that demand for AI hardware and related technology products is contributing to global inflationary pressures.

This AI-driven demand, coupled with the energy shock from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, is expected to push global inflation to 4.7% this year. Central banks, including the European Central Bank, the U.S. Federal Reserve, and the Bank of England, have already raised rates this year in response to inflationary pressures.

Georgieva emphasized that while the energy shock may eventually dissipate, 'AI is for ever,' making it a significant and lasting driver of world trade, competitiveness, productivity, and economic growth.

articles.headline: Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors
body: In this interim final rule (IFR), the Department of Commerce is establishing new rules to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on U.S. technology to threaten U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. First, this rule establishes new restrictions which will apply for exports, reexports, or transfers (in-country) to overseas data centers that remotely supply significant volumes of compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau. These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models. Data centers, foreign foundries, and chip exporters are required to perform robust due diligence on their customers, including any direct or indirect ownership or control by persons in Country Group D:5 or Macau, as part of complying with this new control. The license requirement will not apply to commercial recommender systems, such as those used by online retailers or social media companies, as these functions do not pose the same national security threat. Second, in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs)--countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion. The license requirement for these five countries will not apply to semiconductors destined to companies headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent company is headquartered in, the United States, provided certain reporting requirements are met. Commerce will be actively monitoring for countries that tolerate evasion of this IFR and will consider a range of consequences for such countries, such as import restrictions, new license requirements on advanced semiconductor exports, downgrading the country's status in the U.S. export control regime, and Entity List designations and temporary export prohibitions for foreign persons involved in such activities. Third, this IFR amends the presumptions which front-end chips fabricators and chip packagers face when exporting advanced-node logic chips. These amendments reduce the number of pathways to overcome the presumptions for chip designers located in destinations which face a license requirement for SI chips. This change gives the U.S. government critical oversight over companies headquartered in certain countries that seek to leverage advanced semiconductor production capabilities in third countries. Finally, the IFR formally rescinds the regulations implementing the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule. The AI Diffusion Rule has never been enforced. The regulatory changes in this rule formalize the rescission of the AI Diffusion Rule, which the Department of Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced in May 2025.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
